posts.heading: September 25, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 266 visits and 22 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the most frequent visitors, while Gray Catbird, Northern Flicker, and American Goldfinches were absent from the daily count.

Two feeders were refilled in the late afternoon, specifically the seed-feeder at 18:22 and the nectar-feeder at 18:38. House Finch and White-breasted Nuthatch were recorded daily for the past week.

A Northern Cardinal was visually confirmed 11 minutes before sunrise. By 19:03, a Blue Jay was observed 20 minutes before sunset.

posts.heading: September 24, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 313 feeder visits and 21 species, placing the day above the seven-day average for both metrics. Regulars such as the Northern Cardinal, Tufted Titmouse, and Carolina Chickadee held their usual positions, while the Eastern Kingbird returned after an eight-day absence. Common Grackle, Northern Flicker, and Red-breasted Nuthatch were recorded for the first time at the station, with the grackle also marking its first confident visual sighting.

Audio and visual data captured a consistent mix of daily residents, including Blue Jays and Carolina Wrens, which have been present every day this week. A single Eastern Phoebe was noted perching on a branch, adding to the six-day streak for that species. Downy Woodpecker, Pileated Woodpecker, and Song Sparrow were not recorded, consistent with their sporadic history over the past week.

The day’s activity level sat between the quiet Tuesday and the busier Wednesday of the previous period, reflecting a steady state in station usage. With no changes to feeders or audio sources, the presence of new species is treated as a station record rather than a shift in local bird populations. The numbers align with the consistent baseline established earlier in the week.

posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 321 feeder visits and 23 species, against a seven-day average of 235 visits and 20 species. Carolina Chickadees, Northern Cardinals, and Tufted Titmice dominated both audio detections and visual counts. Tufted Titmice accounted for 155 confirmed visits, while the Carolina Wren showed a significant spike in morning vocalizations.

The Gray Catbird marked its sixth appearance in the last week and the Black-and-white Warbler recorded its only visit during this period. The Red-shouldered Hawk and Pileated Woodpecker were also present, though less frequently. No new audio-only species were detected, and the core group of nine species recorded every day this week remained consistent with their recent history.

Activity spanned the full daylight period, beginning with a Gray Catbird sighting 4 minutes before sunrise and ending with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird 12 minutes before sunset. A Tufted Titmouse was observed perching on the rim of a treat bowl.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 428 feeder visits, more than double the average of the previous week, while detections came in below the recent norm. Tufted Titmice led the visual counts with 203 visits, followed by House Finch and Northern Cardinal, all regulars present on every day of the last seven. Cedar Waxwing returned after a seven-day absence, joining a list of twenty species recorded, including the first visual sightings of Brown-headed Cowbird, Eastern Bluebird, and Field Sparrow at this station.

Eastern Phoebe, which had been recorded daily for the prior week, did not appear today. Other species missing from this day's log include Downy Woodpecker and White-eyed Vireo, both of which were seen on at least five of the last seven days. The audio log captured 251 detections, led by Carolina Wren and Northern Cardinal, with Eastern Towhee also prominent in the afternoon hours.

No changes to feeders or audio sources were noted. A male Ruby-throated Hummingbird was observed perched on the green feeder column near the red nectar feeder. The first visual record occurred six minutes before sunrise, and the last was noted six minutes after sunset.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.
